page: Microsoft Azure F8-4ams_v7 is a constrained-core virtual machine configured with four dedicated physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz on Microsoft Hyper-V. Built on the x86_64 architecture with one thread per core, the system pairs its 4 vCPUs with 64.0 GB of system memory, producing a generous 16.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware features include 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, 32 MB of L3 cache, and instruction support including AVX-512, AVX-VNNI, and AVX512_BF16. The instance includes no bundled local storage and contains no discrete GPUs.

Benchmark data reflects leading single-thread computational strength. In stress-ng single-core tests, the instance scored 3688.19, placing it in the top tier alongside single-threaded gzip compression at 40.54 GB/sec and single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 18.02 GB/sec. Text generation on a lightweight 135M parameter language model achieved top-tier throughput at 342.26 tokens per second. Multi-core performance aligns with expected mid-tier capacity for a 4-core system, yielding a PassMark CPU score of 12460.46 and a stress-ng multi-core result of 14555.95. Uncached memory read bandwidth over 256 MB blocks measured 55.03 GB/sec, supporting 12.69 million Redis SET operations per second.

The 16:1 memory-to-core ratio allows this instance to optimize software licensing models that charge per core, offering high memory density without paying for unneeded vCPUs. The primary architectural tradeoff is the complete absence of local disk drives, necessitating network-attached storage for persistent storage and file systems. Processing larger machine learning models shows limitations, with 7B parameter prompt processing falling into the lower quartile. The instance is suited for memory-intensive caching systems, in-memory databases, batch compression services, and single-thread-sensitive enterprise software.
description: Microsoft Azure F8-4ams_v7 is an x86_64 virtual machine featuring four dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 physical cores operating at up to 4.5 GHz without multithreading. It provides 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding an elevated 16.0 GB per vCPU allocation alongside 32 MB of L3 cache. Benchmarks highlight upper-decile single-thread performance, with exceptional throughput in single-core stress testing, gzip compression, and lightweight language model generation. Overall multi-core throughput and memory bandwidth align with mid-range enterprise averages, sustaining 12.69 million Redis SET operations per second. The server does not bundle local disk storage or hardware accelerators, requiring network storage for persistent operational state. This architecture delivers favorable efficiency for memory-heavy, license-constrained workloads where raw core count is limited but per-core memory and single-thread speed are paramount, including in-memory databases, data compression services, and enterprise cache layers.
